bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42470379 (harfbuzz): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target hb-shape-fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42470379
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `BEInt<unsigned short, 2>::operator unsigned short() const` while `hb_face_create()` sanitized the exact staged 256-byte witness `poc`. The first four bytes are `00 00 01 00`, so `switch (u.tag)` in `OpenTypeFontFile::sanitize()` selects the `DFontTag` arm. In that same union view, those bytes also make `ResourceForkHeader.data == 0x00000100`; bytes 4..7 make `map == 0x00000100`; and bytes 8..11 make `dataLen == 0x20202020`. On the first sanitize pass, `data.sanitize(c, this, dataLen)` accepts the EOF `data` offset at the shallow range check, then fails the target `UnsizedArrayOf<HBUINT8>` array check and falls through to `neuter(c)`. Because the blob is not writable yet, that edit request does not change `data`, but it increments `edit_count`, so `hb_sanitize_context_t::sanitize_blob()` obtains a writable copy and retries. On the second pass, the same `data.sanitize` failure path is neutered successfully, setting `data` to 0 and allowing `map.sanitize(c, this, &(this+data))` to run. `map` is still `0x00000100`, exactly the 256-byte blob length, and `OffsetTo<ResourceMap>::sanitize_shallow()` accepts that offset because `check_range(base, 256)` only validates the span up to end-of-buffer. The helper then invokes `ResourceMap::sanitize()` on a reference at `base + 0x100`. In the vulnerable source, `ResourceMap::sanitize()` computes `const void *type_base = &(this+typeList);` before `c->check_struct(this)` runs, so `this+typeList` dereferences the `typeList` field of that nonexistent `ResourceMap`. The `BEInt<unsigned short, 2>` conversion that reads the 16-bit `typeList` offset performs the out-of-bounds load reported by ASan. The patch resolves the bug by moving `&(this+typeList)` into the right-hand side of `c->check_struct(this) && typeList.sanitize(...)`, so the `ResourceMap` pointer is validated before `typeList` is touched.

source.value_from: The exact 256-byte witness `poc` begins with `00 00 01 00`; at line 515 that value is read as `DFontTag`, so the switch selects the `case DFontTag` arm at line 521 and calls `u.rfHeader.sanitize (c)`.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. The big-endian 16-bit load for `ResourceMap::typeList` reads from an EOF `ResourceMap` reference admitted on the second sanitize pass.
sink.note: ASan reports `READ of size 1` in this function. `typeList` sits 24 bytes into `ResourceMap`, so after step 8 passes `map == 0x100`, step 10 materializes `this == base + 0x100`, and step 11 touches `this+typeList`, this load reads 24 bytes past the 256-byte blob.

root_cause.description: On the second sanitize pass, after `map.sanitize` accepts `map == 0x100`, the vulnerable code eagerly evaluates `this+typeList` before `c->check_struct(this)` can validate that the `ResourceMap` pointer is in-bounds.
root_cause.note: The fix keeps the same base expression but moves it into `typeList.sanitize(...)` on the right side of `c->check_struct(this) && ...`, so the short-circuit check runs before `typeList` is dereferenced on the EOF `ResourceMap` pointer.

coarse_trace.summary: The attacker-controlled bytes `00 00 01 00` are read by `switch (u.tag)` as `DFontTag`, and the selected branch enters the DFont resource-fork sanitizer.

On the first pass, `data.sanitize(c, this, dataLen)` consumes `data == 0x100` and `dataLen == 0x20202020`, accepts the EOF offset shallowly, fails the target-array check, and asks to neuter the read-only `data` field.
The failed first pass records an edit request on a non-writable blob, so `sanitize_blob` obtains a writable copy, retries, and the second pass neuters `data` to 0.
On the second pass, `map == 0x100` is consumed and the shallow range check again accepts an offset landing exactly at end-of-buffer.
The helper invokes `ResourceMap::sanitize` on the EOF reference, and before validating that `this` names an in-bounds `ResourceMap`, the vulnerable code computes `&(this+typeList)`.
The big-endian 16-bit load for `typeList` reads outside the 256-byte blob and ASan reports the heap-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: Source. The first four bytes of the exact witness are `00 00 01 00`, so line 515 reads `u.tag == DFontTag`; the selected branch at line 521 then enters `u.rfHeader.sanitize (c)`.

The left conjunct consumes the DFont header's `data` and `dataLen` fields before `map.sanitize (...)` can run. Because `u.tag` and `u.rfHeader.data` share the union bytes, the same first four bytes give `data == 0x100`; bytes 8..11 give `dataLen == 0x20202020`.
First pass. `sanitize_shallow` accepts `data == 0x100` because `check_range (base, *this)` only requires `[base, base + 0x100)` to fit; with a 256-byte blob, an offset landing exactly at EOF passes.
First pass. `StructAtOffset<UnsizedArrayOf<HBUINT8>> (base, 0x100).sanitize (c, 0x20202020)` fails here because `check_array` cannot fit `dataLen` bytes starting from EOF.

Because step 4 returned false, `OffsetTo::sanitize (...) || neuter (c)` takes the `neuter (c)` arm. On the first pass `may_edit` bumps `edit_count` but denies the write because the blob is not writable, so `data` stays `0x100` and the whole left conjunct remains false.

Seeing the failed first pass with `edit_count && !writable`, `sanitize_blob` obtains writable storage for the blob, sets `writable = true`, and jumps to `retry`, restarting sanitization on the copied buffer.
Second pass. The same `data.sanitize` failure path reaches `c->try_set (this, 0)` again, but now the write succeeds and neuters the `data` offset to `0`, so the left conjunct returns true.

Now line 436 runs on the second pass. It consumes the witness-controlled `map == 0x100`; because step 7 set `data == 0`, `&(this+data)` is the address of HarfBuzz's global `Null(UnsizedArrayOf<HBUINT8>)` object rather than the raw blob EOF pointer.
The present guard for `map` only proves that `[base, base + 0x100)` fits in the 256-byte blob. That admits an offset landing exactly at EOF.

With step 9 accepted and `map` non-null, the helper materializes `StructAtOffset<ResourceMap> (base, 0x100)` and calls `ResourceMap::sanitize (c, d1)` on that EOF reference; no `ResourceMap` struct check has run yet.

Root cause. On the step-10 EOF reference, this line eagerly evaluates `&(this+typeList)` before the next line's `c->check_struct (this)` can short-circuit. The patch fixes the order by deferring `&(this+typeList)` until after the struct check passes.

fine_trace.code: inline bool is_null (void) const { return has_null && 0 == *this; }
fine_trace.note: Evaluating step 11's `this+typeList` first asks whether `typeList` is null. That reads the 16-bit `typeList` field from the nonexistent `ResourceMap`, i.e. 24 bytes past `base + 0x100`.
ASan sink. The big-endian conversion performs the byte load behind step 12's `0 == *this` test and reports the out-of-bounds read in this function.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Commit `67449c39331babb88f7d29d737895d786cd5da33` removes the eager local `type_base` and passes `&(this+typeList)` directly into the right-hand side of `c->check_struct (this) && typeList.sanitize (...)`, so `typeList` is not evaluated on an invalid `ResourceMap` pointer.
sanitizer_ground_truth.evidence_note: The saved ASan stack captures the crashing second pass: `ResourceForkHeader::sanitize` -> `OffsetTo<ResourceMap>::sanitize` -> `ResourceMap::sanitize` -> `is_null()` -> `BEInt<unsigned short, 2>::operator unsigned short() const`. The earlier initial sanitize-pass `data.sanitize` failure, `neuter` request, and `sanitize_blob` retry are not separate ASan frames, but they are directly grounded in the staged vulnerable source and the exact witness bytes `data == 0x100`, `dataLen == 0x20202020`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42470379 run --version vulnerable --expect crash` and reproduced `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `BEInt<unsigned short, 2>::operator unsigned short() const`, matching OSS-Fuzz issue 42470379.

format.name: hb-shape-fuzzer raw DFont-tagged blob
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact 256-byte witness stored in `poc` (SHA-256 `29f886e41f36035f843730917102ab5905961317c458e8da0d10bc99804506da`). Its first 12 bytes are exactly `00 00 01 00 00 00 01 00 20 20 20 20`: bytes 0..3 must still parse as `DFontTag` and, in the `ResourceForkHeader` union arm, also make `data == 0x00000100`; bytes 4..7 must still make `map == 0x00000100`, exactly the blob length; and bytes 8..11 must still make `dataLen == 0x20202020`, which is what forces the initial neuter-and-retry path. In the saved file, bytes 12..255 are all `0x20`. Stage 01 only proves this exact blob; this contract does not generalize to nearby offsets, lengths, or alternative DFont layouts.
